question: E3 follow-up: do the two conditions that moved the map most on gpt-6-luna (open information, unequal stakes) move it the same way on claude-sonnet-5-5 and gpt-6.1-sol? E2's 20 instances, 16 cells (the rule diagonal and every strategy against neutral in both seats).

open_info_gpt_6_luna_E2.model_condition: E2's run of this condition on gpt-6-luna (24 cells; the 16 shared ones are compared)
open_info_gpt_6_luna_E2.prediction: on gpt-6-luna, open information made competing the best unilateral strategy (+9.4 against neutral, p = .047) by exploiting a default partner that could see the competing side's scores, and collaborating the best reply to competing (+6.8, p = .035); the default pair was the most efficient of all conditions (gap 12.3)

open_info_claude_sonnet_5_5.model_condition: claude-sonnet-5-5 through the proxy, thinking disabled; reply cap 1,500 tokens (the first run at 700 lost 78 moves to truncation and was set aside)
open_info_claude_sonnet_5_5.prediction: on the stronger models the default pair reaches the frontier in almost every game, so no unilateral strategy gains more than 3 points over neutral and competing alone no longer exploits the partner (own gain under 3, partner's loss under 5); collaborating and accommodating pairs tie with the neutral pair; competing pairs remain the worst cell

open_info_gpt_6_1_sol.model_condition: gpt-6.1-sol through the proxy, reasoning off
open_info_gpt_6_1_sol.prediction: on the stronger models the default pair reaches the frontier in almost every game, so no unilateral strategy gains more than 3 points over neutral and competing alone no longer exploits the partner (own gain under 3, partner's loss under 5); collaborating and accommodating pairs tie with the neutral pair; competing pairs remain the worst cell

low_stakes_p2_gpt_6_luna_E2.model_condition: E2's run of this condition on gpt-6-luna (24 cells; the 16 shared ones are compared)
low_stakes_p2_gpt_6_luna_E2.prediction: on gpt-6-luna with stakes 1 against 0.3, the high-stakes side did best by collaborating against neutral (68.1 against 57.4) and the low-stakes side's best unilateral strategy was competing (23.1 against 20.5 of 30), its worst accommodating and avoiding (17.1, 17.0)

low_stakes_p2_claude_sonnet_5_5.model_condition: claude-sonnet-5-5 through the proxy, thinking disabled
low_stakes_p2_claude_sonnet_5_5.prediction: the seat asymmetry survives on the stronger models: the low-stakes side still gains nothing by accommodating (own payoff below neutral's) and its joint gain goes to the high-stakes side; but the high-stakes side's collaborating edge over neutral shrinks below 5 points, as the default partner concedes the low-stakes issues by itself

low_stakes_p2_gpt_6_1_sol.model_condition: gpt-6.1-sol through the proxy, reasoning off
